Second, the census records are closer in time to the event: 5 and 15 years after Patrick's birth, respectively, compared to 63 years for the death certificate.

A son-in-law reporting his father-in-law's birth 63 years after the fact, with no firsthand knowledge of the family's Irish origins, would naturally supply the American state where the family had always lived in his experience rather than the Irish birth he never knew about. This is not informant dishonesty; it is the predictable result of secondary knowledge at a great remove from the event.

Ireland is accepted as Patrick Flynn's birthplace.
